chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Minqari, from Ahmad ibn Yunus, from Abu Hashim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The inhabitants of the Fire are eternally in the Fire because their intentions in the world were that if they were to remain in it, they would disobey Allah forever.'
And the inhabitants of Paradise are eternally in Paradise because their intentions in the world were that if they were to remain in it, they would obey Allah forever.
Thus, these and those are made eternal by their intentions.
Then he recited the Words of the Exalted: 'Say, each acts according to his own disposition.'
ai.seo_question: Why are some people eternally in Paradise and others in Hell according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the eternal nature of Paradise and Hell is rooted in the enduring intentions (niyyat) formed during worldly life, where the desire for perpetual obedience or disobedience solidifies one's final abode. This narration uniquely interprets the Quranic phrase 'shakilah' (disposition/manner) in Surah Al-Isra as specifically referring to one's underlying intention, thereby linking psychological intent directly to metaphysical destiny. This perspective underscores the Shia emphasis on intention as the decisive factor in the permanence of the soul's state, moving beyond mere action to the spiritual orientation of the heart.
